text:
I could only read one of the three roundups. WIRED and Runner's World wouldn't load, so these picks come from SoundGuys. It didn't run a dedicated running test, so the running notes are based on each model's features and water resistance.

**Best picks for running**

- **Best clip-on: HUAWEI FreeClip 2, about $200.** It's lightweight and rated IP57, so sweat and rain aren't a problem. It's pricey, and the fit takes some getting used to.
- **Best value: Soundcore AeroFit 2, about $80 at Amazon.** The ear hooks adjust to four positions, and it's rated IP55. Reviewers found the touch controls too sensitive. One owner got about 6 hours per charge against the 10 hours claimed.
  - A third-party deal site, Dealectric, lists a $25.99 discount with code AFSC20 on Soundcore's own store. That would make it about $104 from a $129.99 list price. I didn't verify this, so check it at checkout: [Dealectric listing](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2). Amazon's $80 price is lower than that anyway.
- **Best overall sound: Nothing Ear (Open), about $99 at Amazon.** It has strong bass for an open design, an IP54 rating, an EQ in its app, and multipoint pairing.
- **Best for endurance runs: Shokz OpenFit 2, about $180.** It gets about 11 hours of battery, and its physical buttons work with gloves. The OpenFit 2+ ($200) improves call quality.
- **Best features: Sony LinkBuds Open, about $158.** It gets about 9.5 hours of battery and has a stabilizer fin. It's rated IPX4, so it's less sweatproof than the others.

**My recommendation:** For most runners, I'd go with the Soundcore AeroFit 2 for its price and secure fit. If you want the most secure, sweatproof option and don't mind spending more, get the FreeClip 2.

The Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 (bone conduction) and Bose Ultra Open Earbuds also came up in your search, but I couldn't read their reviews, so I'm not ranking them.

Source: [SoundGuys best open-ear headphones](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/). I didn't have direct purchase links for most of these, so search the model names at Amazon or the brand's store.
